newsitem.title: USA: Continental CEO slams American pacts.
newsitem.headline: Continental CEO slams American pacts.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc Chief Executive Gordon Bethune Monday slammed the alliances AMR Corp's American Airlines is signing with Latin American and other airlines.

"You can call it an alliance, because it sounds friendly. But where I come from, we say you can dress a pig up and call it anything you want, but it is still a pig," he told the International Airline CEO conference organized by Aviation Management Services and its consultant Robert Booth.
The agreements between American and airlines such as the TACA group of airlines in Central America have been slowly grinding through the regulatory process, Bethune said.

"But they are finding that their strategy isn't working because it's not allowed under the Dept. of Justice's merger guidelines. Their pursuit of alliances with Avianca, TACA and British Airways is getting no further than the paperwork," he said.
The anti-competitive problem created "is not my opinion, it is the Department of Justice rules," he said.
Continental has long battled American Airlines, the dominant regional carrier, for market share in Latin America.
"Continental is aggressively building and maintaining its position as the second-largest carrier in Latin America," he said.
Continental is hoping to purchase Aerolineas Argentinas.
"We expected that decision two weeks ago," he said. But he said airline officials were meeting Monday in Argentina and might announce a decision.
American has also expressed interest in the Argentinian carrier.
